# Lattice Memory Certification

Question: bound complete-string BB84 recovery when arbitrary collective encoding retains a quantum register of bounded dimension and unlimited classical information; compile the result conditionally through existing LWE-based remote preparation.

Authoritative routes:
- Continuous explanatory account: learning/report/Lattice_Memory_Certification_Report.pdf
- Report source and rebuild instructions: learning/source/Lattice_Memory_Certification_Report.tex and verification/REPORT_BUILD.md
- Learning entrypoint: learning/README.md
- Exactly 30 project-defined milestones (14 background, 16 narrative): learning/MILESTONES.md
- Single educational anchor, selected Watrous sections, notation and worked example: learning/WATROUS_BRIDGE.md
- Story and dependencies: science/README.md
- Exact models and statements G, C, L: science/model.md
- Classical refinement, discrimination, PGM identity, normalized hypercontractivity, rank: science/guessing-bound.md
- Computational simulation, pass weighting, efficiency and LWE boundary: science/cryptographic-certification.md
- Achieved attack, logarithmic order, complete resource boundary: science/lower-bounds-and-resources.md
- Lists, tolerated errors, erasure timing and honest-noise limitations: science/errors-and-losses.md
- Attribution and finite prior-bound comparison: references/RELATED_WORK.md and references/references.bib
- Reproduction scope and commands: verification/README.md, verification/verify.py and verification/check_learning.py

Preserve these distinctions: ideal information-theoretic bound versus computational classical-verifier protocol; rank only in pure conditional branches; quantum versus classical refinement labels; ordinary trace versus normalized Schatten norm; exact-string versus list acceptance; honest logical storage versus total physical workspace; inverse-polynomial versus negligible compiled soundness. Neither test counts nor a single accepted run certify a theorem or deterministic memory size. No external peer review, exhaustive priority search, hardware implementation, or cryptographic hardness test is asserted.
